findings.evidence: `IsMulCommutative.of_comm` is the intended constructor: `mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Semigroup.lean:185` — `alias ⟨_, IsMulCommutative.of_comm⟩ := isMulCommutative_iff`; Mathlib itself uses it for exactly this purpose at `mathlib/Mathlib/FieldTheory/Galois/Abelian.lean:76-77` (`haveI : IsMulCommutative Gal(↑(K ⊔ L)/F) := .of_comm fun a b ↦ ...`).
findings.fix: Add one named declaration next to the definition, e.g. `theorem isMulCommutative_of_commute (hab : ∀ σ τ : L ≃ₐ[K] L, Commute σ τ) : IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := .of_comm fun σ τ ↦ (hab σ τ).eq`, and use `letI := isMulCommutative_of_commute hab` at all eight sites.
findings.issue: The commutative structure derived from `hab` is constructed inline eight times as `⟨⟨fun σ τ ↦ (hab σ τ).eq⟩⟩`: ArtinMap.lean:89 (`artinElementAway`), :102, :113, :136 (`artinHomAway`), :152, :164, :237 (with `commute_of_intermediateField hab M`), and FieldTheory/Galois/Abelian.lean:40. The nested anonymous constructor reaches through `IsMulCommutative`'s `Std.Commutative` field layout instead of using the API constructor, so all eight sites break together if that mixin is refactored.

findings.evidence: ArtinMap.lean:136 vs :152 carry the same `⟨⟨fun σ τ ↦ (hab σ τ).eq⟩⟩` term; the proof of `artinHomAway_apply` is `(rfl)` (line 154), and `artinSymbol_eq_mk_artinElementAway` closes with `exact (ConjClasses.mkEquiv.apply_symm_apply _).symm` after `rw [artinElementAway]` (lines 102-104), where `ConjClasses.mkEquiv` needs the `CommMonoid` derived from that instance (`mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Conj.lean:223,236`).
findings.fix: Use the single named `isMulCommutative_of_commute hab` from the previous finding in both the definition and this statement so the two terms are the same declaration, and add a one-line comment on `artinHomAway_apply` saying it is the defining equation of `MonoidHom.mk'`.
findings.issue: `artinHomAway_apply` puts a copy of the inline instance construction into its own *statement* (`letI : IsMulCommutative (L ≃ₐ[K] L) := ⟨⟨fun σ τ ↦ (hab σ τ).eq⟩⟩` on line 152) and is proved by `(rfl)`. Since `letI` inlines, the proof holds only because that copy is textually identical to the one inlined in `artinHomAway` at line 136; editing either one silently breaks the `rfl`, and any downstream `rw`/`simp` with this lemma must match the copied instance term rather than a synthesized one. The same coupling makes `artinSymbol_eq_mk_artinElementAway` (line 102) depend on its `have` matching the `letI` inside `artinElementAway` that `rw [artinElementAway]` exposes. Neither is commented.

summary: The proofs are short and readable, but the `IsMulCommutative` instance driving the whole construction is rebuilt eight times as a nested anonymous constructor `⟨⟨fun σ τ ↦ (hab σ τ).eq⟩⟩`, bypassing Mathlib's `IsMulCommutative.of_comm`, and one copy sits inside a public lemma statement that is then closed by `rfl` only because the copy matches the one inlined in the definition.
